scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): agrees that easily-swayed leaders accomplish little while arguing that listening can be a strength; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Leaders who change course with every shift in the public mood can seem to have no direction at all.
Some people argue that any leader easily influenced by shifts in popular opinion will accomplish little.
I largely agree that leaders need firmness, but I believe listening to public opinion is not always a weakness.
First, a leader who follows every change in opinion usually achieves very little.
Real goals take time, and a leader who keeps reversing course never finishes anything.
For example, a leader who abandons a good plan at the first complaint will leave it half done.
This shows that constant changing weakens both progress and public trust.
People also lose respect for a leader who seems to have no firm beliefs of her own.
Difficult but necessary decisions are often unpopular at first and require steady courage.
To this extent, the statement rightly warns against leaders who simply follow the crowd.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why listening can be a strength

sentences.text: Second, however, paying attention to public opinion is not always a weakness.
In a democracy, a leader is meant to listen to and represent the people.
Consider a leader who wisely changes a harmful policy after the public points out its real dangers.
Such flexibility shows good judgment rather than weakness or lack of direction.
A leader who ignores all opinion can become as harmful as one who follows it blindly.
The skill lies in knowing when to stand firm and when to listen and adjust.
Responding to opinion, then, is not always a failing but can be a strength.
In conclusion, a leader swayed by every shift in opinion will indeed accomplish little.
But wisely listening to the public can be a real strength rather than a weakness.
The best leaders hold firm to their goals while still listening carefully to the people they serve.
